beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Aditya Raj. This is DayThread, my final project. You're hearing a synthesized voice reading my script.

beats.narration_text: DayThread will be a check-in assistant for home care. It will remember what a client says from one day to the next. When something concerning comes up, like a fall mentioned in passing, it will show the client's exact words to a care coordinator, who decides what happens next.

shot.visual_intent: Day 1 and Day 2 pages on a thread; a terracotta dot on Day 2; an evidence slip travels to the coordinator's desk. Labels: `Day 1` · `Day 2` · `coordinator`.

beats.narration_text: Why it matters: a coordinator shouldn't have to reread every conversation, and a summary alone can't be trusted. In my October test, Claude's summaries all kept the fall, but nine of ten changed what the client meant.

shot.visual_intent: a check-in page, an arrow, a summary page; two tallies appear: `kept the fall: 10 of 10` and `meaning changed: 9 of 10`. Caption: replay run 2026-10-25, synthetic data, fictional client.

beats.narration_text: Others have built parts of this. Lifeline sells automatic fall detection, and says it doesn't detect every fall. DailyCall makes daily AI phone calls with summaries for families, and says it can't guarantee every safety concern is detected or interpreted correctly.

shot.visual_intent: two plinths: a pendant with a response tower (`Lifeline`), a phone with a summary page (`DailyCall`). No logos. Caption: from each company's own documentation, read 2026-10-14.

beats.narration_text: I'm not claiming they lack anything. DayThread's focus is narrower: every concern linked to the client's own words, a separate check of the raw transcript, and a person who decides before anything leaves the system.

shot.visual_intent: the two plinths shrink left; a third, `DayThread · planned`, slides in: three linked pages, a scan line, a small closed gate.

beats.narration_text: Here's how I'll build it. First, a delegation contract: each step must hand the next one something it can check, and if the check fails, the work stops. I'll write the contract and its tests before Claude writes any code.

shot.visual_intent: a contract page with a seal; three steps joined by arrows; a check mark lands on each handoff; the last handoff gets a stop bar. Labels: `contract` · `handoff` · `stop`.

beats.narration_text: The raw transcript will be saved and can't be edited. Every claim in memory must quote it word for word. And an approval only counts if the evidence and the action haven't changed since the coordinator saw them.

shot.visual_intent: an append-only binder; a page linked to the memory drawers by a quote line; a closed gate with a lock. Labels: `append only` · `quoted` · `bound to what was seen`.

beats.narration_text: Each check-in will run as a loop with a turn budget. It stops when the conversation ends or the budget runs out, never just because the model says it's done.

beats.narration_text: The separate check will be a small open model, DistilRoBERTa, downloaded from Hugging Face and fine-tuned by me to flag concerning sentences. It reads the raw transcript, never the summary, so it fails differently from the thing it checks.

beats.narration_text: All data will be synthetic, with fictional clients. Claude will write the training sentences under labelling rules I set, and I'll spot-check them. I'll write the held-out test sentences myself, before any training, and lock them away.

beats.narration_text: Do I have what I need? Claude Code through my existing account, so no API credits. The base model is a free download, so no new account. Training will run on my laptop, in Python, with PyTorch and S-Q-Lite.

beats.narration_text: The order: the contract and tests, then the test set, then training data, then the checker, then the loop, memory and review page. Last, one run on the held-out set, before December twentieth.

beats.narration_text: To evaluate the checker, I'll compare it with a simple keyword list and with the model before training, on the held-out set. I'll write the pass mark down before I look. If it doesn't beat the keyword list, that's the result I'll report.

beats.narration_text: Then one controlled failure. My test never dropped the fall on its own, so I'll force a summary that drops it. It passes only if the separate check catches it and a coordinator reviews it.
